items.title: The AI Transparency Trap
items.excerpt: Scholarly Kitchen argues that neither the absence of AI nor disclosure of AI use guarantees trustworthy research, questioning publishers' reliance on AI-disclosure policies.
items.rationale: Fresh (11-02) on-whitelist piece challenging the AI-disclosure policies publishers are now writing; directly shapes editorial policy.

items.title: AI에 출판계 '혼란'…저작권·이용료 논란에 표준계약서 손질
items.excerpt: 생성형 AI 학습용 출판 데이터의 적정 이용료 논쟁이 본격화하면서 출판계가 AI 관련 조항을 담아 표준계약서 손질에 나섰다.
items.rationale: Concrete action: Korean publishing is rewriting its standard author contract with AI clauses — changes what authors sign.

items.title: Your writing was flagged as AI. What does that actually mean?
items.excerpt: As editors turn to imperfect AI detectors such as Pangram to screen submissions, writers who say they were falsely accused are left wondering what triggered a positive result.
items.rationale: Credible, practical explainer on how submission-screening detectors flag writers and what a positive result means; new angle (false positives) vs the earlier Pangram CEO story.

items.title: Korean cartoonists take demands for AI consent, copyright safeguards to UNESCO
items.excerpt: Korean comic creators called at UNESCO for rules requiring artists' consent before their work is used to train AI models, plus copyright safeguards.
items.rationale: New event: Korean comics creators bring an AI-training consent demand to an international body (UNESCO); comics/webtoon spread.

items.title: Project Hail Mary Author Says He 'Might Be Among the Last Generation of Fully Human Writers'
items.excerpt: Andy Weir says he may be among the last generation of fully human writers, comparing AI to tools like hammers, forklifts and race cars.
items.rationale: Freshest item in the pool; a bestselling novelist's stance on AI as a writing tool — high reader interest, distinct from prior author-commentary cards.
